rounds.proof_sketch: num_blocks = (128 + 256 - 1) / 256 = 383/256 = 1 (original) vs (128 + 256 + 1) / 256 = 385/256 = 1 (mutant). Both formulas yield identical results because 128 is not a multiple of 256. The mutation only affects cases where size ≡ 0 (mod 256), which cannot occur with fixed size=128.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the ceiling division formula from (n + d - 1) / d to (n + d + 1) / d. These formulas differ only when n is a multiple of d (256 in this case). With the fixed input shape of [128, 1], size is always 128 elements after flattening. Since 128 is not a multiple of 256, both formulas compute num_blocks = 1. The kernel launches identically, processes the same 128 elements, and produces bitwise-identical results. No tensor value can change the size parameter.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE under fixed-shape contract. Would require size to be a multiple of 256 (e.g., shapes like [256, 1] or [512, 1]) to expose the difference where mutant allocates an extra block.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for block/grid sizing formulas should include test configurations where input sizes align with block boundaries (multiples of block_size). The standard ceiling division formula (n + d - 1) / d is sensitive to off-by-one errors specifically at boundary conditions.
